\begin{chapstatus}{Roadmap of this chapter}
By the end of the chapter you can:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item compute the capacity of a memory from its address and data lines
\item describe the interface between processor and memory during a load
\item explain memory-mapped input/output
\end{enumerate}
It builds on: little-endian byte order (Chapter~\ref{ch:information}). Next: Chapter~\ref{ch:storage}.
\par\smallskip\textbf{Looking back, looking ahead.} Since Lecture 02, lw t1, 0(t0) has read a word at an address computed from t0. Today that address is the one placed on the address bus, register plus constant. Lecture 19 calls this base plus displacement and compares it with the other addressing modes. \emph{Recall:} In lw t1, 8(t0), which address goes on the address bus?
\end{chapstatus}
